narratives.Overview:
## Summary

The canonical TypeScript deft update path can mutate managed files and later stage them without first proving that the consumer repository starts in a safe Git state. On a dirty checkout, this can overwrite same-file work or mix updater changes with an existing index.

This recut keeps the measured safety problem and replaces the earlier overlap/occupancy design with one bounded contract:

- default update is whole-repository fail-closed on dirty or undeterminable Git state;
- one new, closed-form dirty escape may proceed only with automatic staging disabled;
- every planned mutation, including the version-matching repair path, is covered by the same pre-write gate;
- occupancy serialization and stale-default classification are not owned here.

Accepted design-critique input: successor lean 5530287902, verified-claims table 5530741147, and synthesis 5530746969.

## Measured failure

A Directive 0.109.1 to 0.111.0 refresh was run from a stale dirty feature checkout. The updater replaced the managed deposit and auto-staged framework files into the existing index before session identity and occupancy conflict became visible. Most staged files duplicated a change already present on the default branch; generated fields accounted for the remaining delta.

At the pinned recut SHA, the TypeScript refresh still reaches destination writes before its first Git porcelain read. The status helper collapses Git failures to an indeterminate result that update-side consumers currently treat as empty/clean. The version-matching alreadyCurrent branch can still repair projections, update Git configuration, and stage files.

## Chosen contract

### 1. Read-only operation plan

Before any updater write, derive the complete planned mutation set for both payload-changing and version-matching repair paths from the existing mutation-ledger/port-record machinery.

Planning must itself be write-inert. It must not update the project, index, common Git configuration, user home, OpenClaw state, or another external path. Any currently excluded writer must either join the recorded plan or run only after preflight succeeds.

### 2. Three-state Git preflight

Read repository state as exactly one of:

1. clean;
2. dirty, with measured staged, unstaged, unmerged, rename-source/destination, and untracked paths;
3. undeterminable, with the Git failure preserved.

Use NUL-delimited porcelain with all untracked files and repo-root-relative paths. Resolve nested project roots explicitly for reporting. Never map a missing Git binary, non-repository state, safe.directory refusal, locked/corrupt index, parse failure, or other non-zero Git result to clean.

### 3. Default refusal

If the complete operation plan is non-empty, default deft update refuses on either dirty or undeterminable before the first updater write. The default gate is intentionally whole-repository; it does not claim that current code can safely classify dirt as unrelated.

Initial install is outside this rule. This issue does not recreate the frozen Go installer contract or its blanket --force/--allow-dirty behavior.

### 4. Explicit dirty escape

Add one new, exact option: --allow-dirty-no-stage.

When selected:

- dirty state and the planned mutation set are printed before confirmation/apply;
- automatic git add is disabled for the entire run;
- structured output records that the dirty escape was active and why staging was skipped;
- commit guidance uses explicit updater-written paths and never suggests a bare commit that could absorb a pre-existing index;
- unknown or misspelled update options fail parsing instead of being ignored.

The option is explicit risk acceptance, not proof that existing dirt is unrelated. It does not waive an undeterminable Git state.

### 5. Honest outcomes

- no-op: the full plan is empty; destination and index remain unchanged.
- updated: preflight succeeded and the reported ledger-derived mutation set was applied.
- refused: dirty default, undeterminable Git state, or another pre-write safety failure prevented every updater write.
- recoverable post-write failure: apply succeeded partly or fully but staging/reconciliation failed. This state reports written paths and does not claim refusal, no-op, or clean success.

A version marker match is not sufficient for no-op. If alreadyCurrent still has a repair plan, it follows the same preflight and mutation rules as any other update.

## Structured output

- Populate the existing dirty_tree and dirty_files fields from measured state; remove hardcoded clean literals.
- Preserve XY/index state and both rename endpoints in the structured fact surface.
- Use stable refusal codes, including distinct dirty and Git-undeterminable outcomes.
- Report whether the dirty escape was active, whether staging was disabled, and every ledger-derived path written, deleted, or staged.
- Dry-run and live execution must derive from the same operation plan and report the same preflight result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clean, dirty, and undeterminable Git states are distinct typed results; only clean proceeds by default.
- [ ] Dirty staged, unstaged, untracked, unmerged, renamed, and mixed fixtures refuse before every updater write by default.
- [ ] Git command absence/failure, non-repository state, safe.directory refusal, and locked/corrupt index never read as clean.
- [ ] Pre-write refusal leaves the deposit, managed projections, generation token, worktree, index, common Git configuration, and external user-state paths unchanged.
- [ ] --allow-dirty-no-stage is parsed as a closed option, never auto-stages, reports measured dirt, and produces path-scoped commit guidance.
- [ ] A misspelled or unknown update option exits non-zero with usage guidance.
- [ ] A true no-op has an empty full-operation plan and leaves destination plus index unchanged.
- [ ] A version-matching repair with a non-empty plan is treated as a mutation and passes through the same preflight.
- [ ] A post-write staging/reconciliation failure reports a named recoverable state and the actual written paths; it is not reported as refusal or success.
- [ ] Existing dirty_tree and dirty_files JSON fields contain measured values in success, refusal, dry-run, and override paths.
- [ ] Initial-install behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] Focused updater, staging, JSON, nested-project, and packed-consumer tests cover the contract.

## Non-goals

- Classifying dirty paths as safely unrelated.
- Holding an updater-exclusive occupancy/common-Git-dir lease across linked worktrees.
- Solving stale checkout versus default-branch generation ordering.
- Modifying the frozen Go installer or reusing its --force semantics.
- Automatic commit, push, pull-request creation, or merge.
- General preservation or rollback of arbitrary uncommitted consumer work.

## Related work

- #4120 owns generation rewind/default-tip ordering.
- #2849 owns broader dirty-state checkpoints across ownership-changing handoffs.
- #1458 is observable prior art for pre-swap placement and structured dirty fields, not the implementation contract.
- #3378 and #3394 provide mutation-ledger and ledger-scoped staging primitives.

## Verdict on the refutation target

The load-bearing half survives re-verification: there is no cleanliness or target-validity preflight anywhere before the first dest write on the canonical TypeScript path. `runRefreshDeposit` (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/refresh.ts:680`) runs exactly three pre-write refusals — legacy layout (#1912), deposit symlink containment (#2305, `assertDepositContained`), and C3 on the incoming package — then calls `copyContent` (`replaceTree`) at line 760. No porcelain read occurs until line 860, long after the swap, and the only `git status` consumer on that path is the post-hoc side-effects reporter.

Four clauses of the target do not survive as written. Three of them fail on evidence at the pinned SHA, not on taste.

## Findings — blocks-the-design

### blocks-the-design — 1. The cleanliness probe the update path already owns fails open, so "fail closed" is asserted rather than delivered

Evidence: `gitPorcelain` (`packages/core/src/story-ready/git.ts:7`) returns `null` for ENOENT, for any non-zero git exit, and for any other throw. Its own docstring says "Maps to config error (exit 2) at the evaluator — fail closed, never assume clean" — but the update path's consumer does the opposite: `frameworkRefreshSideEffects` maps `null` to `{ files: [], crlfOnlyCoreFiles: [] }` (`refresh.ts:462-463`), and `stageFrameworkPaths` maps `null` to "skip" (`hygiene.ts:1024`). Both readings on the update path treat undeterminable as clean.

Failure mode: a container CI image or a `PATH`-stripped agent shell without `git`, or a repo where `git status` exits non-zero (index.lock held, corrupt index, `safe.directory` refusal). The probe returns `null`, the guard reads "clean", and the full `replaceTree` proceeds against the very state the guard exists to refuse.

Disposition consequence: the acceptance criterion cannot be satisfied by wiring the existing helper in earlier. The lean must specify a three-state probe (clean / dirty / undeterminable → refuse) and say which of the two existing fail-open call sites keeps its current behaviour, or the criterion binds against the codebase's own idiom.

### blocks-the-design — 2. The overlap partition is computed on repo-root-relative paths against project-root-relative matchers, so it silently inverts for any non-root project

Evidence: `git status --porcelain` emits repository-root-relative paths regardless of cwd. Measured, not asserted — scratch repo, deft project at `sub/`, run from `sub/`:

```
$ git -C /tmp/dc4158-probe/sub status --porcelain
 M sub/AGENTS.md
 M sub/nested/app.txt
```

`isInstallerManagedPath` matches the exact string `AGENTS.md` (`hygiene.ts:81`) and `isCoreStagePath` matches the prefix `.deft/core/` (`hygiene.ts:912`). `classifyChangedEntries` (`refresh.ts:386`) uses those same prefixes on porcelain output. Nothing under `packages/core/src/init-deposit/` resolves `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (verified: zero hits in that directory).

Failure mode: consumer repo with the deft project at `tools/app/`, operator mid-edit on `tools/app/AGENTS.md`. The dirty entry is `tools/app/AGENTS.md`; the overlap classifier sees no planned-path match, calls it unrelated, honours the new structured override, and `writeAgentsMd` plus `git add` do exactly what #4158 reports. The guard reports "no overlap" on the one file it was built to protect.

Disposition consequence: "overlapping dirty paths refuse; unrelated dirty paths may override" is not implementable on the current path basis. Either the criterion names a repo-root ↔ project-root normalisation as part of the contract, or the partition must be dropped in favour of the whole-tree gate #1458 actually shipped.

### blocks-the-design — 3. A successful update leaves precisely the overlapping set dirty, so the proposed rule deadlocks the second run with no escape

Evidence: leaving framework files uncommitted is the designed end state, not an error. `printRefreshSideEffects` (`refresh.ts:493`) prints "the refresh and framework payload swap left these framework files with uncommitted changes"; `printCommitGuidance` (`hygiene.ts:1311`) then hands the operator a five-step branch-commit-push-PR-merge recipe to land them. `.deft/GENERATION.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.prettierignore`, `Taskfile.yml`, `.githooks/`, `.agents/` are all on `installerManagedMatchers()` (`hygiene.ts:79-140`) — i.e. all of them are planned paths on the next run.

Failure mode: operator runs `deft update`, is interrupted before finishing the five-step commit recipe, and re-runs. Every dirty path now overlaps a planned path. Under the target's sentence, overlap refuses and the override does not reach it. The refusal is permanent until the operator completes exactly the step they were interrupted during, and the tool offers no way through. #1458 had `--force` for precisely this; the target removes it for the overlap class specifically.

Disposition consequence: the overlap class needs either an escape or an explicit carve-out for "dirty because a prior run of this tool wrote it" (the mutation ledger from #3378/#3394 can distinguish this). A criterion that hard-refuses the tool's own documented residue is not shippable.

### blocks-the-design — 4. "Without resurrecting `--force`" rests on a false premise, and enforcing it routes blocked operators onto the binary that is documented as unpatched

Evidence at `ed58d30f`, three separate points:

- `--force` was never dropped. `cmd/deft-install/hygiene.go:36,48,61,133-152` still carries the #1458 whole-tree gate with `--force` / `--allow-dirty` as the escape. It is frozen (`packages/core/src/legacy-bridge/`, `verify:go-freeze`), not deleted, and it is still built and released (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci-lane.yml`).
- The bridge is still a live consumer surface. `refresh.ts:691-692`: "The npm CLI never migrates -- the frozen Go bridge does (stage 1), then the npm path (stage 2)." `content/UPGRADING.md:479` and `:632` still publish `deft-install --yes --upgrade --repo-root . --json` as the upgrade recipe.
- `--force` is also live in TypeScript, on an adjacent path. `content/UPGRADING.md:366`: `task migrate:xbrief` "requires a clean working tree unless you pass `--force`", implemented at `packages/core/src/xbrief-migrate/migrate-project.ts:422,465` over `checkGitClean`.

Failure mode: `content/UPGRADING.md:490` records that the frozen Go installer is explicitly **not** patched for the #2305 symlink-escape refusal and is risk-accepted won't-fix. A consumer hard-blocked by the new TypeScript refusal follows the still-published `deft-install --upgrade --force` recipe and completes the same upgrade through the one path with no deposit-containment check. The net effect of adding a no-escape TypeScript refusal is to move dirty-tree upgrades onto the unpatched binary.

Disposition consequence: the "no `--force`" constraint must be restated. Either the frozen bridge's gate is documented as the escape of record (and its #2305 exposure accepted for that case), or the TypeScript path carries an escape and the constraint is about spelling and structured reporting rather than about the existence of an override. As written the clause is a factual claim about the tree that the tree contradicts.

## Findings — sharpens-framing

### sharpens-framing — 5. "Index collision refuses before the first dest write" cannot hold, because the index mutation is the last step

Evidence: the only index write on the update path is `depositStagePaths` → `stageFrameworkPaths` → `containedDestExec(git add)`, at `refresh.ts:868`, after every dest write. A pre-write index probe is separated from the index write by the entire `replaceTree` + reconcile + projection sequence.

The current failure is also silent, which the criterion should name: `stageFrameworkPaths` returns `{ staged, error }` (`hygiene.ts:1017-1052`), and `depositStagePaths` destructures only `{ staged }` at `hygiene.ts:1448` — the error is dropped on the floor. `buildUpdateSummaryJson` then reports `success: true` with `staged_paths: []` (`refresh.ts:582-623`). A concurrent `index.lock` today produces a successful-looking update that staged nothing.

Disposition consequence: split the criterion. A pre-write probe on observable index state (staged entries overlapping planned paths), plus a named recoverable post-write staging failure in the epic's own three-outcome vocabulary. One pre-write sentence cannot cover a mutation that happens ~200 lines later.

### sharpens-framing — 6. The already-current cell already stages consumer-authored content, and the target's last clause does not reach it

Evidence: `refresh.ts:867` — `if (!alreadyCurrent || effects.files.length > 0)`. On the already-current path, `strategy` is literally `"no-op"` (`refresh.ts:724`), yet `writeAgentsMd`, `writeAgentHookDeposit`, `writeSlashCommandDeposit`, `writeConsumerGitHooks`, `ensureInitGitignoreLines`, `ensurePrettierIgnoreLines` all still run (`refresh.ts:822-853`), and any path they touch enters the ledger and is then `git add`ed.

Failure mode: consumer at the current version, with their own prose edits in `AGENTS.md` outside the managed section. `deft update` rewrites the managed region, `git add AGENTS.md` stages the whole file including the unrelated prose, and the JSON reports `already_current: true`, `strategy: "no-op"`. No upgrade occurred, and consumer-authored content was staged.

Disposition consequence: the target's stale-vs-already-current clause is about *labelling* the cell. The measured harm on that cell is index mutation, not the label. The criterion for the no-op cell should be "dest **and index** unchanged" — #4159 already words it that way; this issue's sentence does not, and this issue is where the guard lands.

### sharpens-framing — 7. `dirty_tree` and `dirty_files` are hardcoded literals today, so the structured surface is actively lying

Evidence: `refresh.ts:612-613`, unconditional `dirty_tree: false, dirty_files: []` in `buildUpdateSummaryJson`. These are the #1453 Go-parity keys.

Failure mode: any automation reading `deft update --json` today receives `dirty_tree: false` on a dirty tree. This is a live false negative independent of whether the guard ships.

Disposition consequence: promote this to its own acceptance criterion rather than folding it into "structured output". It is a one-line defect with an existing key, testable now, and it is the difference between "the guard reports" and "the guard is observable".

### sharpens-framing — 8. Three clean-tree predicates already exist; a fourth override spelling needs a recorded why

Inventory at the pinned SHA:

| Predicate | Location | Shape | Escape |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checkGitClean` | `packages/core/src/migrate-preflight/index.ts:71` | `CheckResult` PASS/WARN | `--force` at `migrate-project.ts:422,465` |
| `checkGitClean` | `packages/core/src/release/git.ts:31` | `[boolean, string]` | `--allow-dirty` (release pipeline) |
| `checkDirtyTree` | `cmd/deft-install/hygiene.go:137` | `dirtyTreeAdvisory` | `--force` / `--allow-dirty` |

Note the third is *whole-tree*: `checkDirtyTree` blocks on any non-empty porcelain, with no overlap partition. The target's "restores the #1458 safety contract" is therefore inaccurate in both directions — #1458 refuses more (any dirty path) and permits more (`--force` escapes everything, including overlap). The proposal is a different contract, not a restoration.

Disposition consequence: say "a new two-class contract, stricter than #1458 on overlap and looser on unrelated paths" rather than "restores #1458", and name which of the three existing predicates is being reused or why none composes. Otherwise reviewers will validate the wrong invariant.

### sharpens-framing — 9. Occupancy is a different state store and a different check; it does not belong inside a porcelain preflight

Evidence: `.deft/occupancy.json` is git-ignored by the installer itself (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/gitignore.ts:40`), so it is structurally invisible to any `git status --porcelain` probe. Grep across `packages/core/src/init-deposit/` finds zero occupancy references outside that ignore-list entry — occupancy is not consulted anywhere on the update path. The predicates already exist: `liveOccupancyOnTree`, `occupancyAdmission`, `occupancyLiveness`, `isOccupancyExpired` (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:276,383,324,341`).

Failure mode: a criterion that says "dirty index or worktree … occupancy conflict … refuse" as one sentence invites one implementation over one probe. A porcelain probe can never see an ignored lease file, so the occupancy half would silently no-op while the tests for the dirty half pass.

Disposition consequence: two facts, two checks, two refusal codes. Also note #4159 words this as "occupancy / owner-liveness **for the duration of the mutation**" — this issue's sentence drops the duration, and a point-in-time refusal does not deliver it (see the swarm lens below).

### sharpens-framing — 10. Pre-write refusal is not zero-write outside the project root

Evidence: `UPDATE_DRY_RUN_EXCLUSIONS = ["openclaw-home-skills"]` with the label "Excluded from dest plan (not yet captured by the port)" (`refresh.ts:987-990`). `runRefreshDeposit` calls `depositOpenClawSoftRebindSkill` and `depositOpenClawL2ProductCommands` at `refresh.ts:828-833`, and `installOpenClawPin` (`packages/core/src/doctor/openclaw-skills.ts:382-413`) uses raw `mkdirSync` / `rmSync` / `renameSync` against the `$HOME` OpenClaw state dir — outside `containedDestExec`, so `isPortRecordMode()` (`packages/core/src/fs/contained-write.ts:696`) does not suppress them.

Failure mode: this matters concretely for the *implementation shape* of the guard. The cheapest correct way to compute the planned-path set is a record-mode pass (see road-not-taken); that pass writes `$HOME` OpenClaw skills before the refusal is issued.

Disposition consequence: state the zero-write claim as project-root-scoped, or make the excluded site a criterion of this issue rather than a shrinking label.

## Findings — footnote

### footnote — 11. "Auto-stages into unrelated work" overstates the mechanism, and the precision changes the tests

Since #3394 the stage set is ledger-bound: `depositStagePaths` intersects this-run ledger paths with the installer-managed allowlist plus `.deft/core` (`hygiene.ts:943-973` with `depositStagePaths` at `hygiene.ts:1412-1457`). The updater never `git add`s an arbitrary unrelated file. The two real mixing channels are (a) same-file overlap inside allowlisted paths — `package.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore` are all on the allowlist and all consumer-editable — and (b) `printCommitGuidance` step 2, a bare `git commit -m "chore(deft): update framework payload"` with no pathspec, which commits whatever else was already in the index. Acceptance criteria written against "stages unrelated files" will pass on a build that still produces the reported harm.

### footnote — 12. #1453's initial-install carve-out has no TypeScript counterpart

`dirtyTreeGate` (`cmd/deft-install/hygiene.go:122-128`) encodes a CRITICAL invariant: "an initial install never probes the tree and can never be blocked." `runInitDeposit` and `runRefreshDeposit` are separate entry points, so scoping to `update` is natural — but the invariant is currently recorded only in frozen Go, and the shared `depositStagePaths` call at `init-deposit.ts:308` is the seam where it could leak. Worth one sentence in the criteria.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered: this target changes shared consumer Git state (worktree, index), the deposit, and proposes to read occupancy.

**Concurrency / TOCTOU.** The proposed guarantee is point-in-time at t0; the index write happens at t1 after a full-tree replace of the deposit. Nothing holds a lock for `[t0, t1]`. `containedDestExec` does not serialise on `.git/index.lock` and there is no `index.lock` handling anywhere in the tree (grep: zero hits). Two co-resident agent sessions in one worktree — the ordinary swarm shape — can interleave `replaceTree` and `git add`. A pre-write refusal makes the honest-outcome claim *look* satisfied while the window is unchanged. #4159's "for the duration of the mutation" wording is the correct one and this issue drops it. The deterministic control, if one is wanted, is an occupancy mutation lease held across the write plus a re-probe immediately before `git add` — not reviewer attention and not a single pre-write read.

**Untrusted input.** Deposit content arrives from the resolved content package; `assertDepositContained` (#2305) is the existing containment control on the TypeScript path and runs before the first write. The lens finding is finding 4: the frozen Go bridge is documented at `content/UPGRADING.md:490` as *not* carrying that control, and a no-escape TypeScript refusal makes that binary the recovery path. Adding a refusal without an escape moves traffic from the patched path to the unpatched one. That is a security consequence of a safety criterion, and it should be recorded on this issue rather than discovered by a consumer.

**Identity.** `installOpenClawPin` writes under `$HOME` (finding 10), i.e. outside the project blast radius the "zero-write" claim is scoped to. A `$HOME`-scoped write executed during a refusal path crosses from project state into user state.

## Road not taken

I considered three bases for the "planned paths" set the overlap partition needs, and rejected two.

- **Static allowlist** (`frameworkStagePaths` / `installerManagedMatchers`) — rejected: over-broad. It names every path the installer *may* manage, so on a typical repo it declares overlap with `package.json` and `.gitignore` on nearly every run, collapsing the two-class rule into finding 3's deadlock.
- **Hand-rolled write-set prediction** — rejected: it is a second source of truth against `replaceTree` + reconcile + eleven projection writers, and it drifts the moment a writer is added.
- **Record-mode ledger** (chosen) — `runInPortRecordMode(() => runRefreshDeposit(...))` already produces the exact `MutationSummary` with dest writes suppressed at `contained-write.ts:696`, and `emitDryRunPlan` (`refresh.ts:993`) already does exactly this on `--dry-run`. The planned-path set is therefore *measurable* today, not approximable. This is the one place where the proposal is under-ambitious rather than over-ambitious: the criteria should say "overlap is computed against the recorded port plan", which makes the partition exact and folds refusals into the ADR-004 dry-run vocabulary the epic already wants. The `openclaw-home-skills` exclusion (finding 10) is the known hole in that basis.

## Steelman of the position I am arguing against

The strongest defence of the target as written: overlap-only refusal with an override for unrelated paths is the only rule that does not regress the ordinary consumer, who almost always has *something* dirty. A whole-tree #1458-style gate would refuse nearly every real upgrade, which is presumably why the Go default was warn-and-proceed for one release (#1453) before flipping (#1458) — and why the TypeScript path never adopted it. On that reading, findings 2 and 3 are implementation bugs in a correct rule, not defects in the rule.

What would flip my verdict on findings 2 and 3: a measurement showing that on real consumer repos the planned-path set (computed from the record-mode ledger, per road-not-taken) is disjoint from the ordinary dirty set often enough that the deadlock in finding 3 is rare — plus a normalisation step making the classifier correct for non-root projects. If both hold, findings 2 and 3 drop to sharpening. Findings 1 and 4 would not move: finding 1 is a fail-open probe regardless of the partition, and finding 4 is a factual claim about `--force` and a routing consequence that no partition changes.

## What I did not do

I did not run the repository test suite. The dispatch is direct-mode and read-only against `ed58d30f`; running vitest in that checkout would write build and cache artifacts there. Every code claim above is from `git show` at the dispatch SHA, and the two behavioural claims about git itself (porcelain path relativity; ignored paths absent from porcelain) were measured in a scratch repository under `/tmp`, shown inline.

## Verdict

The safety premise is supported, but the recorded lean does not yet survive refutation. The pinned tree builds and the four focused suites pass (240/240), so the findings below are design gaps and currently encoded behavior, not an unexplained red baseline.

### blocks-the-design — the occupancy boundary is narrower than the updater's write boundary

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:245-285` makes occupancy worktree-local and treats another worktree's record as residue. `packages/core/src/session/main-worktree.ts:21-49` recognizes that linked worktrees share a common Git directory. Every refresh reaches `writeConsumerGitHooks` (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/refresh.ts:822-836`), which may execute `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts:482-517`). That changes repository-common Git configuration even though the mutation ledger names the lexical worktree path `.git/config`.
